problem: Classical EQA answers one isolated question at a time by exploring from scratch, so it cannot handle several questions that arrive asynchronously with different urgencies, nor reuse observations across questions.
motivation: Real deployments (rescue robots, service assistants) receive multiple questions, including urgent follow-ups mid-exploration. Since physical steps are costly, reducing exploration steps and answering urgent questions first is critical to responsiveness.
key_idea: Formulate Embodied Questions Answering (EQsA) and solve it with ConEQsA: a shared group memory that lets questions be answered directly from past observations, plus an urgency/scope/reward/dependency priority scheduler that decides which question to explore next.
insight: Most of the gain comes from sharing memory and scheduling rather than better single-question perception: accuracy is nearly unchanged (0.65 vs 0.64 Memory-EQA), but NS drops to 0.321 and NUWL to 0.204. In the ablation, replacing priority with FIFO (w/o Priority) raises NS from 0.321 to 0.398 and NUWL from 0.204 to 0.232. Urgency, Reward and Dependency each matter, while Scope matters least (NUWL 0.213 without it).
method: Generator/Parser: the Generator emits a time-stamped question stream (initial at t=0, follow-ups delayed); the Parser (LLM) attaches urgency u_i, scope (local/global), target set and dependencies to each question at arrival.
Group Memory: stores observation images with semantic records (room, caption, object boxes, 3D positions from YOLOv11 + Qwen2.5-VL-7B + depth), indexed by CLIP+FAISS and shared across all questions.
Finishing Module: on arrival, queries Group Memory and answers directly if the evidence suffices (zero exploration steps); otherwise the question goes to the Question Pool.

Question Pool/Planner: the priority P = w_u*(-ln(1-u)) + w_s*Scope + w_r*Reward (number of other questions with overlapping targets) + w_d*Dependency (DAG ready/pending); the top question is selected, with preemption on new arrivals.
Targeted Exploration: Explore-EQA-style question-conditioned frontier exploration on a 2D semantic map, with VLM relevance scores weighting frontiers; exploration starts from the current pose.
Stopping/Answering Modules: a VLM confidence estimator over top-K retrieved memory decides when to stop; a VLM then answers the multiple-choice question from the retrieved evidence.

setting.backbone: GPT-5-mini (frozen, main VLM), GPT-OSS-20B (non-vision LLM), YOLOv11, Qwen2.5-VL-7B (semantic annotation), CLIP+FAISS retrieval
setting.training_data: none (training-free; priority weights tuned once on a validation split)
setting.action_space: frontier-based waypoint exploration with a collision-free planner
setting.privileged: none (urgency labels are used only for evaluation; agent infers urgency from text)

numbers.extra: 40 HM3D scenes, 5 questions each; average over all 40 scenarios

numbers_note: The benchmark is the authors' own CAEQs and has no official split names, so 'test' is used as a placeholder. Values are printed as fractions, not percentages.
results: On CAEQs, ConEQsA reaches Acc 0.65, DAR 0.09, NS 0.321 and NUWL 0.204. The strongest baseline, Memory-EQA, gets Acc 0.64, DAR 0.00, NS 0.410 and NUWL 0.474 (a 57% NUWL reduction for ConEQsA). Explore-EQA gets Acc 0.62, NS 0.472 and NUWL 0.551.
limitations: Bounded by single-question EQA components (perception, navigation, answer accuracy); accuracy is only 0.65 and the system is not yet practical in the wild
Inference latency is about 5 min per question (under 3 min with parallel API calls); the benchmark is small (40 scenes, 200 questions) and simulation-only
Exploration is single-threaded; the priority weights are hand-set; only two baselines are compared, and accuracy gains are marginal
